blocks.text: 7 January 2027. Boat trip to Bartolomé Island

Galápagos Islands — boat trip to Bartolomé Island

Leave the hotel early by bus for the Itabaca Channel, where a yacht will be waiting.

Today you’ll explore the Galápagos archipelago, with its volcanic landscapes, white-sand beaches, clear ocean waters and plants and animals found nowhere else.

On the two-hour crossing to Bartolomé, you can have breakfast on board and take in the ocean views. Dolphins and other marine animals are often seen near the yacht in the early morning.

On arrival, walk to the island’s summit, a climb of about 30 minutes. The trail crosses a volcanic landscape that looks like the surface of another planet. From the viewpoint, you’ll see one of the Galápagos’ best-known panoramas: Santiago, North Seymour, Baltra, Santa Cruz, Rábida and Chinese Hat, as well as Pinnacle Rock, a remnant of an ancient volcanic formation.

After the walk, there’s time to relax on the beach and snorkel.

During the trip, you may spot Galápagos penguins, sea lions, marine iguanas, sea turtles, reef sharks, rays, sea stars and colourful tropical fish. The clear waters around the island are well suited to swimming and watching marine life.

Lunch on board is included.

Return to Puerto Ayora in the afternoon. The evening is free to explore the town, visit its restaurants and souvenir shops, or relax by the waterfront.

Accommodation: Hotel Fiesta (3-star).

Meals: breakfast and lunch.

8 January 2027. North Seymour or South Plaza

Your itinerary is subject to confirmation after booking. The two routes offer different ways to experience the Galápagos’ wildlife and landscapes.

Option 1: North Seymour Island and Las Bachas Beach

In the morning, transfer to the Itabaca Channel and board a yacht. The crossing to North Seymour takes about an hour.

The island has a volcanic landscape and groves of silver-grey palo santo trees. It’s one of the best places in the archipelago to watch birds and marine animals.

On the walk, look for blue-footed boobies, frigatebirds with bright red throat pouches, marine iguanas, sea lions, pelicans and other Galápagos wildlife. Many of the animals are unafraid of people, so you can often see them at close range.

After the walk, have lunch on board the yacht.

Continue to Las Bachas Beach on the north coast of Santa Cruz. Visit a lagoon where flamingos are sometimes seen, then relax on the white-sand beach and snorkel in the turquoise water. You may see sea turtles, rays, sea lions and a variety of tropical fish.

Return to Puerto Ayora at around 16:00. The rest of the day is free.

Option 2: South Plaza Island

Leave the hotel for the Itabaca Channel and board a yacht. The crossing to South Plaza, one of the archipelago’s most scenic small islands, takes about an hour and a half.

Bright red and green vegetation contrasts with white-sand beaches, volcanic rocks and clear turquoise water. The island is home to numerous sea lion colonies, marine iguanas and distinctive bird species.

On the walk, look for blue-footed boobies, frigatebirds, tropicbirds and swallow-tailed gulls. From the island’s highest point, you can watch the waves break against the volcanic cliffs.

Continue to Punta Carrión, one of the best places to snorkel. You may swim alongside rays, reef sharks, Galápagos sharks, sea turtles and hundreds of colourful fish.

Lunch on board is included.

Return to the hotel. The evening is free.

Accommodation: Hotel Fiesta (3-star).

Meals: breakfast and lunch.
